thread:
anna: heads up — we're getting a steady trickle of customer escalations for hosted inference in euw1. p99 latency and 5xx rate spiked ~16:28Z, multiple reports mention auth failures and timeouts, and one customer says their billing meter jumped. opening here for triage. :eyes:
monitor-bot: ALERT hosted-api.euw1 SLO: p99_latency > 3s for 15m, 5xx_rate=1.2% (threshold 0.5%). incident_id=INC-171905
support-bot: New support ticket #SUP-9882 linked: customer reports repeated 502s on /v1/infer and timeouts on streaming. sample payload attached.
ben: on it. can someone paste a minimal repro curl + headers from the ticket? also which routes are seeing the most 5xx?
claire: paste from customer:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-XXXX" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-1", "input":"short"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer``` they say it times out after ~12s or returns 502. tried from euw1 region only.
ben: thanks. running quick log query in euw1:```logs.query("env:euw1 AND http.status_code >= 500 AND http.route:/v1/infer | count by http.status_code, upstream_service")``` will share results in a sec.
ben: result: spike dominated by 502 from upstream runtime-proxy, some 504s when kv-cache misses spike. top upstream: runtime-v2 (70%), grpc-proxy (20%), inference-hotpath (10%).
mike: this looks like an upstream handshake/reset pattern we saw last week. any TCP RSTs in the proxy logs? also check client keepalive settings.
anna: I can see a pattern: 502s cluster between 16:25-16:40, correlated with a small surge of requests from a single org id (acct_999). billing shows a temporary quota bump for that org around same time.
ben: can someone fetch a trace id for a 502 request? need to see where it fails (gateway vs runtime). trace sampling for 502s?
claire: from support logs: sample trace id `trace-euw1-0a1b2c3d`. customer included full headers; token looks OK (not expired).
ben: pulling trace https://traces.internal/trace-euw1-0a1b2c3d — gap between gateway span and runtime span (no downstream spans). suggests gateway attempted connection and got no reply or connection reset.
mike: looking at proxy metrics: increased connection churn to runtime-v2 around same window, with elevated `connect_failures` and `tls_handshake_errors`. could be runtime_v2 nodes rolling or oom-restarts. checking node logs.
ben: node health: runtime-v2-12 had an OOM event at 16:24 and restarted; rolling impacted capacity briefly. autoscaler didn't immediately replace traffic; resulted in short tail latency and some 502s.
anna: that maps to customer repro time. billing spike from acct_999 likely increased concurrent requests causing pressure during restart.
claire: customer says they were retrying aggressively (500ms backoff) which may have made the pressure worse.
ben: short-term mitigations: 1) open incident and run canary fallback to warm model variant, 2) throttle per-org concurrent requests for hosts showing excessive retries, 3) add temporary routing to runtime-v1 for acct_999. thoughts?
mike: agree. also increase probe frequency for runtime pools and tune autoscaler cooldown to replace nodes faster on OOM.
anna: created incident INC-171905, assigned to ben, pinged infra oncall. @mike can you take lead on the kernel/node OOM follow-up? :wave:
mike: on it. I'll post node-level logs and kernel OOM details in the incident. initial hypothesis: memory leak after recent decoder update + spike from acct_999.
ben: I'll push a short-term routing rule and per-org concurrency cap for acct_999. also adding an alert for upstream connect_failures threshold.
claire: support will notify the customer that we identified a transient runtime restart plus retry amplification; asking them to pause retries while we mitigate.
monitor-bot: NOTE: set traces.sample_rate=100% for service=hosted-api.euw1 for 30m (requested by ben) to capture full spans for repro.
ben: follow-ups: add structured logging for upstream connect errors (include upstream node id), add a dashboard panel for per-org concurrency + 5xx correlation, and a billing rule check to alert on unusual quota bumps.
anna: reassigning to postmortem owner: ben. please include timeline, root cause, mitigation, and long-term fix (autoscaler tuning, memory leak patch, per-org throttling).
claire: customer updated: they saw reduced 5xx after 17:00Z, thanks team. closing ticket when incident postmortem is done. :white_check_mark:
ben: thanks everyone. I'll post a short incident summary and the queries we used in the incident channel.
